_comment: Tariff orders slice 2 (v361). Every pair on tariffs_prices, tariffs_growth, tariffs_china, tariffs_authority, econ_trade and cost_living for the sixteen executive documents in db/exec-action-seed.json that carry a tariff or trade key, where the pair printed nothing under its row in the President's drawers: 37 pairs. Each line is stored once in consistency.js _DOS_EXEC_EFFECT under the TARIFF ORDERS SLICE 2 marker, keyed by the document and the issue, and is written only from that pair's own stored `plain`, `rationale` or `counts` and the document's stored title. `term` is the stored words the line carries and `termIn` names the field they are in. No line is a sibling key's line or a vote's line on the same subject, and nothing is summed. The vote-line table (_DOS_EFFECT) is not touched. No score, mapping, direction or standing is read from or written to here.

excluded.why: The day-one affordability directive is not a tariff or trade document: it carries no tariff or trade key, so it is outside this slice and keeps its blank row.
The housing-permitting order is not a tariff or trade document: it carries no tariff or trade key, so it is outside this slice and keeps its blank row.

rows.title: America First Trade Policy
rows.line: Directed Commerce, Treasury and the Trade Representative to investigate persistent goods trade deficits and recommend remedies.

rows.title: Imposing Duties To Address the Flow of Illicit Drugs Across Our Northern Border
rows.line: Imposed duties on goods from Canada by executive order under emergency economic powers, with no rate schedule enacted by Congress.

rows.title: Imposing Duties To Address the Situation at Our Southern Border
rows.line: Imposed duties on goods from Mexico by executive order under emergency economic powers, with no rate schedule enacted by Congress.

rows.title: Imposing Duties To Address the Synthetic Opioid Supply Chain in the People's Republic of China
rows.line: Imposed an extra across-the-board duty on goods from China, after finding ordinary tariff authority inadequate.
rows.term: across-the-board duty on goods from China

rows.title: Imposing Duties To Address the Synthetic Opioid Supply Chain in the People's Republic of China
rows.line: Set the China duty rate by executive order under emergency economic powers, rather than under a rate schedule enacted by Congress.

rows.title: Adjusting Imports of Steel Into the United States
rows.line: Ended every country exemption and quota that had displaced the steel tariff, restoring the duty across steel imports.
rows.term: restoring the duty across steel imports

rows.title: Adjusting Imports of Steel Into the United States
rows.line: Closed the arrangements named partners had used to ship steel outside the duty, to rebuild domestic steel capacity.

rows.title: Adjusting Imports of Steel Into the United States
rows.line: Restored the steel duty with no offsetting relief for the American manufacturers and builders who buy steel.

rows.title: Further Amendment to Duties Addressing the Synthetic Opioid Supply Chain in the People’s Republic of China
rows.line: Doubled the China tariff from 10 percent to 20 percent, finding Beijing had not moved against the fentanyl trade.

rows.title: Imposing Tariffs on Countries Importing Venezuelan Oil
rows.line: Claimed the power to tariff any country that buys Venezuelan oil, at a rate and against a target chosen by the executive branch alone.

rows.title: Regulating Imports With a Reciprocal Tariff To Rectify Trade Practices That Contribute to Large and Persistent Annual United States Goods Trade Deficits
rows.line: Imposed a baseline duty on nearly every trading partner, finding persistent goods deficits had hollowed out domestic manufacturing.

rows.title: Regulating Imports With a Reciprocal Tariff To Rectify Trade Practices That Contribute to Large and Persistent Annual United States Goods Trade Deficits
rows.line: Set reciprocal tariff rates by executive order under emergency economic powers rather than under a rate schedule enacted by Congress.

rows.title: Regulating Imports With a Reciprocal Tariff To Rectify Trade Practices That Contribute to Large and Persistent Annual United States Goods Trade Deficits
rows.line: Put duties on nearly the whole import base with no offsetting relief for household purchasers.

rows.title: Regulating Imports With a Reciprocal Tariff To Rectify Trade Practices That Contribute to Large and Persistent Annual United States Goods Trade Deficits
rows.line: Assigned China one of the higher country-specific rates in its annexed schedule, citing non-reciprocal trade practices.

rows.title: Regulating Imports With a Reciprocal Tariff To Rectify Trade Practices That Contribute to Large and Persistent Annual United States Goods Trade Deficits
rows.line: Used import duties as the instrument for reshoring manufacturing and rebuilding supply chains.

rows.title: Regulating Imports With a Reciprocal Tariff To Rectify Trade Practices That Contribute to Large and Persistent Annual United States Goods Trade Deficits
rows.line: Charged a duty on imported consumer goods from nearly every trading partner, with nothing offsetting it for households.

rows.title: Modifying Reciprocal Tariff Rates Consistent With the Economic and Trade Arrangement Between the United States and the People’s Republic of China
rows.line: Kept the higher China tariff rates suspended for a further twelve months under a negotiated trade arrangement.

rows.title: Modifying the Scope of the Reciprocal Tariffs With Respect to Certain Agricultural Products
rows.line: Pulled a list of agricultural products out of the reciprocal tariff and ordered refunds of duties already collected on them.

rows.title: Modifying the Scope of the Reciprocal Tariffs With Respect to Certain Agricultural Products
rows.line: Narrowed the reciprocal tariff’s coverage, citing current domestic demand and current domestic capacity to produce certain products.

rows.title: Modifying the Scope of the Reciprocal Tariffs With Respect to Certain Agricultural Products
rows.line: Took the reciprocal tariff back off imported coffee, bananas, beef and other farm goods, so it stopped showing up in grocery prices.

rows.title: Ensuring Affordable Beef for the American Consumer
rows.line: Raised the 2026 beef import quota by 80,000 metric tons of lean trimmings, finding domestic supply would not meet demand.

rows.title: Ensuring Affordable Beef for the American Consumer
rows.line: Let more beef enter at the low in-quota tariff rate instead of the high over-quota rate, to hold a grocery price down.

rows.title: Ending Certain Tariff Actions
rows.line: Ended the emergency-powers tariffs on China, ordering agencies to stop collecting them as soon as practicable.

rows.title: Ending Certain Tariff Actions
rows.line: Switched off the whole emergency-powers tariff program at once, the reciprocal tariff among them.

rows.title: Ending Certain Tariff Actions
rows.line: Ended collection of the emergency-powers duties and provided for refunds of duties already paid.

rows.title: Imposing a Temporary Import Surcharge To Address Fundamental International Payments Problems
rows.line: Imposed a temporary 10 percent surcharge on imported articles under the balance-of-payments provision of the Trade Act.

rows.title: Imposing a Temporary Import Surcharge To Address Fundamental International Payments Problems
rows.line: Re-imposed broad import duties the day the previous program ended, under a different statute, so the barrier stayed up without a gap.

rows.title: Imposing a Temporary Import Surcharge To Address Fundamental International Payments Problems
rows.line: Put a surcharge on nearly all imported articles, carving out critical minerals, energy, fertilizers, medicines, some food and electronics.

rows.title: Imposing a Temporary Import Surcharge To Address Fundamental International Payments Problems
rows.line: Placed a surcharge on imported consumer goods generally, more than a year after the directive to bring those costs down.

rows.title: Adjusting Imports of Pharmaceuticals and Pharmaceutical Ingredients Into the United States
rows.line: Set a 100 percent duty on imported medicines, its own findings placing the bulk of covered supply outside the country.

rows.title: Adjusting Imports of Pharmaceuticals and Pharmaceutical Ingredients Into the United States
rows.line: Rested on a national-security finding about foreign dependence for medicines and directed continued negotiation of agreements.

rows.title: Adjusting Imports of Pharmaceuticals and Pharmaceutical Ingredients Into the United States
rows.line: Put a border charge on imported patented medicines, exempting generics, biosimilars and a list of specialty therapies.

rows.title: Strengthening Customs Enforcement
rows.line: Ordered Homeland Security to require importers of record to hold domestic assets or larger bonds and disclose beneficial ownership.

rows.title: Strengthening Customs Enforcement
rows.line: Tightened who may act as an importer of record so duties owed are actually collected.

rows.title: Declaration of Emergency and Authorization for Temporary Duty-Free Importation of Phosphate Fertilizer From Morocco
rows.line: Declared an emergency and let Moroccan phosphate fertilizer enter duty-free for up to eight months, waiving countervailing duties.

rows.title: Declaration of Emergency and Authorization for Temporary Duty-Free Importation of Phosphate Fertilizer From Morocco
rows.line: Chose duty-free foreign supply over the tariff for a fertilizer shortfall, finding domestic capacity would take time to build.

rows.title: Declaration of Emergency and Authorization for Temporary Duty-Free Importation of Phosphate Fertilizer From Morocco
rows.line: Waived a duty on phosphate fertilizer during the spring application window, citing supply-chain disruption and rapid price increases.
